questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has <math><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> capacitance. One of its two plates is given <math><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> charge and the other plate, <math><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> charge. The potential difference developed across the capacitor is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Charge inside capacitor =1μC
V=QC=1×10-61×10-6=1 volt

questions.q: Two capacitors of capacitances <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>C</mi></math> are charged to potential differences <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>V</mi></math>, respectively. These are then connected in parallel in such a manner that the positive terminal of one is connected to the negative terminal of the other. The final energy of this configuration is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Charge on C=CV
Charge on 2C=2C2V

From charge conservation, 2C(2V)-CV=(C+2C)V'
Common potential, V'=V
Final energy, Uf=12CV2+12×2CV2=32CV2

questions.solution:
Ceq=C1+C2C3C2+C3

Ceq=Aε02 d+K1 Aε0 d×K2 Aε0 dK1 Aε0 d+K2 Aε0 d

Ceq=Aε02 d+Aε0 dK1 K2 K1+K2=Aε0 d12+K1 K2 K1+K2

questions.q: Two capacitors having capacitance C1 and C2 respectively are connected as shown in figure. Initially, capacitor C1 is charged to a potential difference V volt by a battery. The battery is then removed and the charged capacitor C1 is now connected to uncharged capacitor C2 by closing the switch S. The amount of charge on the capacitor C2, after equilibrium, is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The initial charge on the capacitor C1 will be Q=C1V. If after closing the  switch the charge flown through the circuit is q, the charge on C2 will be q and C1 will be Q-q. The potential across the capacitors will be same. Hence,

Q-qC1=qC2⇒q=C2QC1+C2⇒q=C1C2C1+C2V

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $1 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is charged to a potential difference of 20 V . The distance between plates is $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. The energy density between plates of capacitor is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \text { Energy density } & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0\left(\frac{V}{d}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(8.85 \times 10^{-12}\right)\left(\frac{20}{10^{-6}}\right)^2 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^3 \\ & \simeq 1.8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A bulb and a capacitor are connected in series across an ac supply. A dielectric is then placed between the plates of the capacitor. The glow of the bulb:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2} \& X_C=\frac{1}{W C}$ due to dielectric $\mathrm{C} \uparrow \Rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}} \downarrow \Rightarrow \mathrm{Z} \downarrow$ So, current increases $\&$ thus bulb will glow more brighter.

questions.q: A capacitor with capacitance <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> is charged to <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> . If the plates are pulled apart to reduce the capacitance to <math><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>, how much work is done?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Uinitial=Q22C1
Ufinal=Q22C2
Work done =Ufinal-Uinitial
=Q22C2-Q22C1
=5×10-622×2×10-6-5×10-622×5×10-6 
=254-52×10-6
=154×10-6 =3.75×10-6 J

12CV2=12LImax2   ...1

Equation (1) implies that

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is charged to a potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math>. The flux of the electric field through a closed surface enclosing the positive plate of the capacitor is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The charge enclosed is given by qinc=CV  

Gauss' law states that the flux through any closed surface is equal to the charge enclosed by the surface.

 Using Gauss' law the flux is, ϕ=qinc ε0=CVε0

questions.q: Three capacitors C1=2 μF, C2=6 μF and C3=12 μF are connected as shown in the figure. Find the ratio of the charges on capacitors C1, C2 and C3 respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the above circuit diagram, the equivalent capacitance of the combination of capacitors is, 

Ceq=C1+C2C3C2C3, 

Ceq=2+6×126+12=6 μF

Then, QC1QC2=C1VC2C3C2+C3V=2×(6+12)6×12=12 

and QC2=QC3

So, the ratio of charges are, 1:2:2.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with square plates is filled with four dielectrics of dielectric constants K1, K2, K3, K4 arranged as shown in the figure. The effective dielectric constant K will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
C1 and C2 are in series.

The equivalent capacitance of C1 and C2 is

C12=∈0A2d2K1+d2K2=∈0AdK1K2K1+K2

C3 and C4 are in series

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor filled with a medium of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math>, is connected across a battery and is charged. The dielectric slab is replaced by another slab of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math>. Then the energy of capacitor will
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a dielectric of dielectric constant K is inserted between the plates of a capacitor C0, the capacitance becomes KC0.

Energy stored in a capacitor is given by, U=12CV2. Now,

Ui=12K1C0V2 and Uf=12K2C0V2

⇒ΔU=Uf-Ui=12K2-K1C0V2

Percentage change in the energy will be,

ΔUUi×100=12×5×C0212×10×C02×100=50%

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Two metallic spheres are charged to the same potential. One of them is hollow and another is solid, and both have the same radii. Solid sphere will have lower charge than the hollow one.

Reason R : Capacitance of metallic spheres depend on the radii of spheres.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential of a conducting sphere is given by V=KQR 

As in case of metallic sphere either solid or hollow, the charge will reside on the surface of the sphere. Since both spheres have same surface area, so they can hold equal charge.

∴Q1=Q2

The capacitance of a metallic sphere depends only on its radius. It does not matter whether the sphere is hollow or solid.

Hence, A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A capacitor is discharging through a resistor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>. Consider in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, the energy stored in the capacitor reduces to half of its initial value and in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, the charge stored reduces to one eighth of its initial value. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that in the discharging circuit the charge is given by,

q=q0e-tRC ⇒tRC=lnq0q

In time t1 the energy stored reduces to half. Hence, q122C=12×q022C⇒q0q1=2. Therefore,

t1RC=ln2=12ln2.

In time t2 the charge stored reduces to 18th of initial value. Hence, q2q0=18. Therefore,

t2RC=ln8=3ln2.

Hence,

t1t2=12ln23ln2=16

questions.q: Using a battery, a 100 pF capacitor is charged to 60 V and then the battery is removed. After that, a second uncharged capacitor is connected to the first capacitor in parallel. If the final voltage across the second capacitor is 20 V, its capacitance is : (in pF)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
New potential $=\frac{\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0}{\mathrm{C}_0+\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{3}$
$\begin{aligned} & 3 \mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0=\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0+\mathrm{CV}_0 \\ & 2 \mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0=\mathrm{CV}_0 \\ & \mathrm{C} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{C}_0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> is charged by a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> battery. The capacitor is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged identical capacitor such that one plate of uncharged capacitor connected to positive plate and another plate of uncharged capacitor connected to negative plate of the charged capacitor. The loss of energy in this process is measured as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged capacitor, then there is loss of energy in the form of heat as charges flow from higher potential to lower potential.

So, heat ∆H=12C1C2C1+C2 V1-V22 

As the other capacitor is identical therefore charge is equally divided.

=12C22C(100-0)2

=12900×10-62×104=94 Joule

=2.25 Joule.

Hence, the value of x=225.

questions.q:
The displacement current of 4.425 μA is developed in the space between the plates of parallel plate capacitor when voltage is changing at a rate of 106 V s-1. The area of each plate of the capacitor is 40 cm2. The distance between each plate of the capacitor is x×10-3 m. The value of x is ,
(Permittivity of free space, ε0=8.85×10-12 C2 N-1 m-2) _______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement current is given by id=ε0dϕEdt

Or id=ε0ddtEA, where E=qAε0

Or id=ε0ddtqAAε0=dqdt=ddtCV

Or id=CdVdt=ε0AddVdt

Putting the values, we have 

4.425×10-6=8.85×10-12×40×10-4×106 d

d=2×10-6×10-4×106×40

d=80×10-4=8×10-3 m

Hence, value of x=8.
